advice.rising: Water is likely to come up about {{rise_m}} m over the next month. A good time to help it recharge: keep farm ponds and recharge pits clear.
advice.uncertain: The forecast could go either way this month. Keep an eye on your own well and plan carefully.
advice.deeper_than_usual: At the last reading ({{date}}), water was {{diff_m}} m deeper than usual for that time of year. Use water carefully; drip or sprinkler irrigation saves water.
advice.rain_deficit: Rain this season is only {{pct}}% of the usual, so less water will soak into the ground. Save stored water.
advice.rain_surplus: Rain this season is {{pct}}% of the usual. Help it soak in with recharge pits, bunds and farm ponds.
advice.extraction_high: In this district {{stage_pct}}% of the usable groundwater is already used each year. Saving and sharing water matters here.

advice.contact_local: For borewell, crop or scheme decisions, talk to your local agriculture office or the GSDA.

help.title: How to use JalVaani
help.intro: JalVaani shows how deep the groundwater is in each district of Maharashtra, what the next month may bring, and how much rain has fallen. The numbers come from CGWB monitoring wells, CHIRPS rainfall, ERA5-Land soil moisture and the CGWB groundwater assessment.

farmer_items.water: Water in the wells now: how many metres below the ground the water is, from the latest CGWB reading, and how that compares with the same weeks in earlier years.
farmer_items.forecast: Next 7, 14 and 30 days: the expected level, a narrow 'most likely' range (right about half the time) and a wide 'could be' range (about 8 times out of 10).
farmer_items.rain: Rain and soil: rain since 1 June compared with the same period in earlier years, and whether the soil is wetter or drier than usual.

gov_items.kpi: The top row counts districts, wells and the main warning signs.
gov_items.map: The map can be coloured by level vs usual, forecast change, extraction, wells or reliability. Tap a district to see it in the panel beside the map, then open its page.
gov_items.table: The table ranks districts with simple rules; each row lists the reasons. It can be downloaded as CSV.
gov_items.needs: 'What we have and what we need' lists the data that exists and the gaps.

glossary.depth: m below ground: how deep the water is in the wells. A bigger number means deeper water.
glossary.usual: Usual: the same weeks of the year in 2023–2025. The records start in 2023, so 'usual' covers only these years.
glossary.range: Could be (wide range): about 8 times out of 10 the real level falls inside it.
glossary.reliability: Reliability: how well past forecasts did here, compared with assuming no change.
glossary.extraction: Stage of extraction: groundwater used ÷ groundwater that can be used each year. Safe < 70%, semi-critical 70–90%, critical 90–100%, over-exploited > 100%.
glossary.provisional: Provisional: recent data that will be corrected when final data is published.
glossary.most_likely: Most likely (narrow range): the darker band around the expected level. It is the typical size of past errors here, so about half the time the real level falls inside it. Same forecast, shown more tightly.

limits.district: District level only: there is no village or taluka detail.
limits.readings: Groundwater readings end on the date shown at the top; newer CGWB readings are not yet published.
limits.advice: The tips are general water-use guidance, not crop, borewell or legal advice.
limits.nodata: Ten districts have no usable well readings, and two have too few; they show rain and extraction only.
